_meta.task: Exact input-closure inventory for jobs/claim-kit and jobs/valla; documentation only.

contexts.A_runner_job_py: what GitHub Actions runs: claim-kit job.py (unit tests, then population check, build, derived check) and valla job.py (valla.build(repo))
contexts.B_agent_cli: claim-kit kit.py prepare/view/apply/batch-check/complete, source_supplement prepare/verify, valla attach (jobs/claim-kit and jobs/valla as invoked from a working checkout)

needed_labels.GENUINELY_NEEDED: read on the normal path of that context
needed_labels.NEEDED_ONLY_FOR_SUBCOMMAND: read only by the listed subcommand(s)
needed_labels.HISTORICAL_BLANKET: declared but not read by current code; evidence given
needed_labels.OPTIONAL_PERFORMANCE_CACHE: extra label for caches that affect time, never results

_meta.method: Full read of the listed modules plus runner scripts. Empirical confirmation by audit-hook trace (sys.addaudithook 'open') of inputs.load_corpus, act_overrides.load, population.validate_inputs, working_text.Index, current_evidence.enrich_current (claim-kit A; 142,532 text declarations) and valla.build (valla A), then comparing the opened set with result_freshness.scope(job) and needs.txt roots. The full claim-kit build() was NOT executed (it would write into jobs/claim-kit/output); the build-time reads (safe_read of the declared texts, decision-sheet assembly) are derived from load_corpus output and static reading.
unverified: Reads of ingest() (REVIEW.jsonl/UPHELD_ACT_RECORDS.jsonl) are static, not traced.
Norton pin verification stops at the first changed pin in this checkout, so the per-file reads of the 20,399 pins are taken from INPUTS.json, not from the trace.
claim-checker and readiness-tracker internals were listed from constants and globs only.
kit.py subcommands outside the requested list (build, next, dossier, sheet, history, status-sheet, overlay-*, assemble, check, status, release) are not inventoried except where they share modules.
Future records may point at any repo path; coverage for such pointers is only as good as the record values observed today.
